messages:
ana_dev: throwing a different idea onto the board: instead of a single rule-matrix in router, what if each compatibility transform is a small signed WASM bundle with metadata? think: hermetic, testable, versioned, and can run in router or remotely in workers. low-risk for private deployments.

ana_dev: motivation: we keep tweaking transforms in code, causing drift and risky deploys. WASM bundles could be built from an RFC artifact, signed by owner, and validated by runtime before activation. also easier to ship tenant-specific variants without inlining heaps of conditionals.

lucas_arch: interesting. difference from coalescer is packaging and attestation. questions: size, perf, and how operators control which bundles run (policy + signature).

kei_runtime: perf note: modern WASM runtimes with AOT compilation are pretty fast, but cold start of a new module matters. we could keep a small LRU cache of compiled modules per router instance. for fast-path rules we'd inline native micro-transforms, but for complex envelope logic a WASM bundle is fine.

kei_runtime: also, sandboxing is a huge win. misbehaving transform won't crash router process. we can restrict memory and CPU and pin execution timeouts.

ana_dev: proposed manifest fields:
```
bundle.yaml:
  id: unwrap-envelope-2026-01
  owner: @ana_dev
  version: v1
  target: router-edge
  match: header X-Client in ["old-sdk"]
  cache_affecting: true
  signed_by: team-compat
  signature: <sig>
```

lucas_arch: governance: require an RFC plus signed manifest for any bundle that runs in hosted. private deployments can opt into unsigned local bundles, but we surface that in console and support contracts. add a policy that any bundle touching cache keys must provide stable-key derivation function and include bundle-version in cache key.

kei_runtime: runtime lifecycle: upload -> validate signature -> dry-run (shadow with compare) -> promote. runtime should reject bundles with unknown cryptographic signer unless tenant-override flag set.

sophia_ops: rollout UX: admin console should show pending bundles, match rate, latency delta, and a safety toggle to quarantine a bundle. when quarantined, router falls back to previous path. we also need a way to force-evict compiled modules across fleet.

jen_sre: SRE constraints: we need SLA guarantees. propose limits: per-request CPU micros per bundle, 99th lat threshold per-route for bundles, and an automatic kill switch when observed errors or p99 delta exceed safe margins for 3 consecutive windows. also synthetic test harness that runs all active bundles against a golden test corpus every 10m.

lucas_arch: security/attestation: signer registry for hosted bundles. bundles signed by vendor or partner must be reviewed and vetted. manifest must include a provenance field (repo, commit, CI job id). prevent arbitrary JS from being uploaded. prefer Rust/Wasm-bindgen or WASI modules.

ana_dev: developer workflow idea: write transform as small Rust crate with a trait like fn transform(req) -> req or transform_and_cmp(req) -> (req,diff). CI builds the wasm, publishes artifact, signs with CI key, and attaches manifest. RFC attaches the test corpus.

kei_runtime: implementation detail: expose minimal runtime SDK: access to headers, body as bytes, a small JSON helper, and a safe logger that writes to structured trace. no network calls allowed inside bundles.

ana_dev: ops concern: how to prevent rules mushrooming? governance: every bundle has TTL and monthly match metrics. automated pruning suggestions for bundles with <3 tenants or <0.05% global match over 60d. owners must provide migration plan.

lucas_arch: compatibility semantics: keep bundle scope narrow: structural transforms and safe normalizations only. behavioral heuristics (e.g., tolerant parsing) should be explicitly gated and require E2E evals.

sophia_ops: observability: emit: bundle_id, version, signer, matched, latency_us, result_hash. also provide a diffing job that records sample input+output for bundle owners to review in console.

jen_sre: incidents: if a bundle causes divergence between mirrored paths we need a fast rollback playbook. action: (1) quarantine bundle (2) force-evict compiled module (3) flip traffic ratio back to native adapter (4) attach request samples to pager with diffs. automate steps 1-3.

kei_runtime: on the perf side, benchmark plan: pick 3 representative bundles: small header-only, medium envelope unwrap, large proto->json convert. measure p50/p95/p99, cold start, memory, and compile time. simulate LRU churn. put numbers in PR.

lucas_arch: legal/privacy: manifests must declare whether transform logs PII or includes payload capture. hosted cannot accept bundles that log full payloads without approval. private deployments can opt in but must surface the risk.

ana_dev: edge case: tenants that insist on custom logic but we want to avoid private bundles in hosted. policy: welcome local bundles for Dedicated/Private, but for hosted we require contributing reusable transform back to compat repo (with maintainer review) or keep it tenant-isolated behind opt-in flag (with billing/SLAs).

kei_runtime: deployment note: ci-bot we need an artifact pipeline: build wasm, run static checks, run golden tests, sign artifact, upload to artifact store. then runtime picks it up via controlled rollout.

ci-bot: pipeline.note: created pipeline stub "wasm-compat-build" (ci:10m). integrates with signing service and publishes to /artifacts/compat-bundles/.

ana_dev: OK next steps I propose:
- draft RFC that specifies manifest, signer registry, runtime SDK, lifecycle, TTL rules, and governance.
- prototype runtime loader with compiled module cache and sandbox. (kei)
- sample transform repo + CI that produces signed bundles (ana)
- console mockups for bundle visibility and quarantine controls (sophia)
- bench plan and synthetic harness (kei + jen)

lucas_arch: I'll take governance and signer registry sections.

kei_runtime: I'll prototype loader and provide perf numbers.

jen_sre: I'll design the synthetic probe suite and rollback automation.

sophia_ops: I'll mock console UX and eviction flow.

ana_dev: sweet. I'll start the RFC draft and link the sample transform repo. tagging folks in the draft when ready. thanks! :sparkles!
